doc.title: Phil Mead interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

title: Favorite browsing room and the loyalty of Hamilton alumni
summary: Mead recalls reading in the browsing room and explains lifelong friendships among Hamilton classmates, including his two sons.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Thank you. You mentioned that this is one of your favorite rooms, we’re in the browsing room.

I spent many, many very happy hours, and I hope I learned something. I did all my reading in this room and it never was terribly popular. I don’t know why. So I could always get a seat and I would bring my David Copperfield or whatever had been assigned and sit here and read and I always have very warm memories. It’s great to be here.
That’s great. And of course you lived on this side of campus because that was the side.
That’s the only side there was, that’s right.

You are the second Hamilton alum I’ve interviewed, the other one was Milt Fillius who was class of ’44. But I asked him and I’m going to ask you, I’ve always been impressed by the loyalty of a significant number of Hamilton alums. And is there a reason for that in your mind?

Well I surely agree with you, it’s remarkable. It was true in my case, I still have very close friendships with many of my classmates and yet both my sons went here, one class of ’88 and one class of ’90 and they have exactly the same friendships. And indeed those friends are now friends of my wife and I. We often on New Year’s Eve will get a call from a Lieutenant JG in Tokyo who is stationed there and is just calling us up to wish us a Happy New Year. And it’s a remarkable thing. And I don’t know if it’s the smallness of the school — I’ve always thought the isolation might have had something to do with it. Certainly when I was there, and I’m not sure it’s a great deal different, your friends were the people that you went to college with because there wasn’t much else around. And so whatever it is it’s been great through my lifetime and it’s great to see it happen to my sons.
